answer: Graph-Distance Admission requires each new agent to route its first transactions through an existing peer, forming a verifiable path in the trust graph. An ember of prior activity must connect it: agents closer than three hops to many fresh nodes get rate-limited. A terrace of established neighbors must co-sign the bridge edge, and that edge expires unless reused. Attackers pay by sustaining many real edges across distinct neighborhoods, since fake clusters stay shallow and costly to keep alive.
